title: Create Indexes
statement:
A web app looks users up by email on every login, and no two users may share a username. Add an index for each job, then check what indexes the table has.

The `users` table has these columns:

- `id`: the user id, the primary key
- `username`: the name the user picked
- `email`: the user's email address
- `created_at`: the day the account was created

Create two indexes:

1. A regular index named `users_email_idx` on `email`.
2. A unique index named `users_username_idx` on `username`.

Then list the table's indexes from the `pg_indexes` view: return `indexname` and `indexdef` for the rows whose `tablename` is `users`, ordered by `indexname`.

Expected output:

```text
CREATE INDEX

CREATE INDEX

     indexname      |                                   indexdef
--------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 users_email_idx    | CREATE INDEX users_email_idx ON public.users USING btree (email)
 users_pkey         | CREATE UNIQUE INDEX users_pkey ON public.users USING btree (id)
 users_username_idx | CREATE UNIQUE INDEX users_username_idx ON public.users USING btree (username)
(3 rows)
```
setup:
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  username TEXT NOT NULL,
  email TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at DATE NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO users (id, username, email, created_at) VALUES
  (1, 'skyler', 'skyler@example.com', '2024-02-11'),
  (2, 'mo_khan', 'mo.khan@example.com', '2024-03-02'),
  (3, 'jdoe', 'jane.doe@example.com', '2024-03-19'),
  (4, 'pixelfox', 'fox@example.com', '2024-05-07'),
  (5, 'rivera88', 'ana.rivera@example.com', '2024-06-23');

hints: `CREATE INDEX name ON table (column)` makes a regular index. Put `UNIQUE` after `CREATE` for a unique one.
The primary key already has an index of its own, so it shows up in the list too.
